doc.title: Mildred Major and Emma Zeno Interview, 1969-03-28

title: Life on St. Claude Street and her father
summary: In New Orleans she lived on St. Claude; her father taught her to embroider, took her on picnics and tried to teach cooking, but left the family early.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now, in, uh, here in the city, New Orleans, I remember living on St. Claude Street. St. Claude between Espanade and Calarick. That's where I can remember my dad coming from there. Yes. Well, he taught me how to sew. She drew for me a picture on a piece of rag and I learned how to embroider on that.
My father used to take me, when he learned small town play music, used to take me on picnets with him. And he learned, he tried to learn me how to cook, but I never learned from him.
I do have a nice time when my daddy was home, but it wasn't too much of a life that my daddy smoked. And he left us rather early. That's not real. Yes. That's about all I can remember was my father.
